_comment: Maps Archipelago ItemInfo.ItemId -> in-game action. Copy to apitems.json (auto-loaded from the app dir) or pass with --items <path>. kind = Inventory | Flag | Clearance | ProgressiveClearance. Ids may be decimal or a 0x-prefixed GID. Every key inside "items" must be a numeric id, so keep notes at the top level like these. NOTE: the single-file client embeds its own copy of apitems.json; a file placed next to the exe (or passed with --items) overrides it.
_comment_flags: A Flag entry takes either "flag": "Name" for the common single case, or "flags": ["A","B"] when one AP item owns several. Every listed flag is granted together and reconciled together. The client relocks any mapped flag Archipelago has not granted, and re-applies the ones it has, on a timer — the game writes these variables itself (a shipped content script sets a whole group of sector flags true), so enforcement has to be continuous rather than one-shot.
_comment_bits: "bits" are elevator UI bits and REQUIRE the UI patch (tools/Ap.Control.Patcher, `apply elevator`); without it they are written but nothing reads them. Stock, the elevator panel derives its floor list from ONE integer = the highest unlocked sector index, which makes the sectors a strict ladder (Maintenance implies Research) and hardcodes Pump Room and Executive as always available. Patched, the panel reads five independent booleans that the client writes instead. Valid names: Research, MaintenanceLobby, Containment, Investigation, MaintenancePumpRoom.
_comment_sector_items: Sector items generally want BOTH "flags" and "bits": the bits decide what the panel OFFERS, the GameFlow flags decide whether the game PERMITS the trip once a floor is chosen. 1101 Research is the simple one-of-each case. 1102 Maintenance owns two of each, because Lobby and Pump Room ('Maintenance Access Corridor') reach the same content and gating only one leaves a back door. 1104 Investigation is already gated by the patch, so adding the item is the whole job when the DLC lands. Executive is deliberately absent: the game forces it available and the patch leaves it always-enabled, since locking the player out of the hub risks a softlock. 1200 shows a plain GameFlow flag with no UI bit — keycards, mission flags, anything not on the elevator.
_comment_clearance: Clearance needs NO entry here: the world mints its ids synthetically as (n << 8) | 0x49 — 329/585/841/1097/1353/1609 for fixed Levels 1-6, and 1865 for Progressive Clearance Level — and the client resolves both from the id (see Utils/ApClearanceIds.cs). Fixed ids carry their level; each Progressive copy received grants the next level (Nth copy -> clearance N, capped at 6). Add an explicit { "kind": "Clearance", "level": N } or { "kind": "ProgressiveClearance" } entry only to override one.
